chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding a man who entered the house of a people without their permission, so their dog injured him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no liability upon them, and if he had entered with their permission, they would have been liable.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on animal liability when a person enters a property with or without permission?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reports that Imam Ali (AS) established this distinction in property law, highlighting that liability for animal-caused injury hinges on the entrant's legal status: a trespasser bears the risk (la daman), while a permitted guest triggers the owner's guarantee (daman). This ruling reflects the broader Shia jurisprudential principle that ownership entails responsibility for hazards within one's domain, provided the victim has a right to be there.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding a man who entered a house of a people without their permission. So their dog injured him. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no responsibility upon them, and if he had entered with their permission, they would have been responsible’.
